insights.insight: Cumulative verified GMV stands at $4,960,678 across 94,620 receipts — the $5M threshold is approximately 3 days out at current pace, marking the first meaningful scale proof point for cryptographically confirmed consumer spend.

insights.topic: Deterministic purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Every receipt in the corpus represents a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent signal — a structural advantage over cookie-based or contextual targeting that charges $5+ CPM to guess whether a purchase occurred.

insights.topic: Grocery and mass retail dominate verified spend
insights.insight: Grocery-supermarkets leads all categories at 1,372 receipts and $61,874 in 14-day GMV; Walmart tops the brand list at 356 receipts, with Kroger, Costco, Aldi, and Safeway all visible — the dataset skews heavily toward high-frequency, everyday spend categories where brand competition is sharpest.

Active metro coverage expanded from 17 to 20 areas within a 24-hour window, suggesting organic user growth is distributing across new markets rather than concentrating in existing ones — relevant for brands evaluating regional targeting reach.

The protocol is processing roughly 340–370 receipts per day with a confirmed burst window between 20:00–00:15 UTC, indicating a stable and predictable data supply rather than episodic or synthetic volume.

The verified sender set spans physical retail, e-commerce, SaaS, and digital goods — meaning the same identity layer that confirms a Walmart grocery run also confirms an Amazon or Stripe transaction, offering a unified purchase graph without device fingerprinting.
